summary: Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. English accompanying the added examples is the supplied project machine translation, copied and cut without retranslation; lexical decisions rest on the Turoyo.
The existing entry already includes Ruhe finden as well as dying, and explicitly marks the preserved w as a learned peculiarity. Neither its wording nor etymological comment is changed.
Jan 3.17/291 uses a learned Syriac frame, including kaḏ and mḏito. The isolated noyaḥ token cannot establish native Turoyo agreement, a new Part act. box or a native nwḥ/nyḥ alternation.
No Jan example is added because the supplied clause is difficult to construe and its English resting interpretation is not sufficient evidence.
Jan 3.17/291: establish the correct reading and syntax of kaḏ, noyaḥ w Omiḏ mḏito wa mqarebwoe. Is noyaḥ a resting predicate, and which Syriac lemma does it represent?
If a native Turoyo resting form is intended, supply its agreement and relation to nwḥ 1 versus nyḥ before adding a Part act. box.
